title: Unit, integration, functional and acceptance tests

videos.script: A test is a program that runs your code and checks what it did. {{definition}} This lesson writes the first ones, for a small project called shipquote. It answers one question for an online bookshop in São Paulo. What does it cost to send this parcel to that CEP? {{project}} You will run a test, watch it pass, and then break the code on purpose to watch it fail. A test you have never seen fail is a test you cannot trust. {{fail}} Then the lesson climbs outwards, one layer at a time. Unit tests check one rule with nothing real around it. Integration tests add a real database. Functional tests start the server and talk HTTP to it. Acceptance tests check a promise in the words of whoever made it. {{layers}} Each layer sees something the one below cannot, and each one costs more. You will measure the cost on this project, and the numbers explain the shape people call the test pyramid. {{pyramid}} The last part is about choosing inputs. Bugs gather where behaviour changes, so the best test sits right on the edge. {{edges}}
